author: /root/limb_sources
methods: Read all 80 stems, correct answers, four-option sets and complete explanations.
Checked the cited actual local Gray 42, Langman 15, Junqueira 16 and Guyton 2026 pages using primary-source text extraction, including full-page follow-up where keyword extraction omitted a passage.
Reviewed near-neighbor overlap against the active existing limb single-best-answer bank; no exact duplicates found in that bounded comparison.
Repaired weak distractors without changing keys, synchronized correct-answer concept retrieval text, and conservatively regraded one-step recognition and simple arithmetic.

Validated all 80 questions against the MCQ schema, reconstructed the flat staging records for concept-catalog schema validation, checked mapped coverage links and verified all 48 retrieval answers against final questions.

books: Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd edition
Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 2026
sourceEvidence.locatorPolicy: Both printed and local PDF locators are retained; the exact new-question source entries were checked. Existing-bank locators remain historical provenance, not a new certification.
sourceEvidence.imagePolicy: All questions are text-only. The three staged PNGs are author source-inspection evidence and must not be published as question assets. Independent review relied on primary text; it does not claim independent visual inspection of those PNGs.

noveltyExamples.distinction: Selective anteroposterior instability with preserved vertical suspension, not simply naming the coracoclavicular ligament.
Suprascapular branch-level localization from infraspinatus-only deficit, not simply naming the supplied pair.
Coordinated proximal and distal radioulnar mechanics, not simply which bone rotates.
PIN motor deficit with preserved radial wrist extension and direction of deviation.
Adolescent physeal barrier and retinacular supply route rather than generic adult neck-fracture vascular risk.
Saphenous arterial branch route rather than the sensory nerve's canal exit alone.
Distal superficial fibular cutaneous lesion with preserved eversion versus a proximal motor lesion.
Initiation versus maintenance in a paired FGF10/AER experiment rather than AER removal alone.

coverageRepairs.reason: A boundary note with no linked concept is not mapped curricular content.
Residual scope limitation is not a mapped concept; avoids false exhaustiveness.

limitations: Book-extension scope is intentional; exact lecture coverage and past-paper provenance are not asserted.
Novelty comparison is bounded to the relevant active limb bank, not an exhaustive proof across every image variant or all organ-system questions.
Coverage is subtopic-level and gap-driven, not every paragraph or all clinical variants.
No level-5 difficulty or arbitrary 50% challenge target is claimed after review.
All question records remain draft for the parent-controlled import; this review is not professional clinical endorsement or patient-management guidance.
